description: Pins the comprehensive-review skill against the failure modes listed in its 'Failure modes to avoid' section. Assertions favour intent over input-echo: keyword lists exclude words trivially present in the prompt, so a response cannot pass by quoting the input back.
model_hint: Any modern instruction-following LLM. Tested informally against Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-4o.

tests.description: A 'looks good, nothing to add' style response is the canonical failure mode; the skill must surface concrete observations instead.
tests.input: Please review this PR description: 'Adds rate limiting to /api/users. LGTM, nothing to add.'

tests.description: Sprawling 'rewrite the whole thing as hexagonal architecture' suggestions are out-of-scope and the skill must keep the review actionable for the current diff. Synonyms ('focused', 'proportional') are accepted to avoid false-fails on natural model phrasing.
tests.input: Review this PR: it adds a 30-line function that validates a date string. The reviewer is tempted to suggest rewriting the entire validation layer.

tests.description: Speculation without a specific reference is a soft-failure pattern; the response must point at a file/line/function or use an explicit anchoring construct. Input-echo words ('Map', 'lifetime', 'process') are deliberately excluded — they don't verify anchoring, they just verify the model repeated the prompt.
tests.input: Review this PR: it adds a Map<string, number> that grows for the lifetime of the process. Decide whether to flag a memory concern.

tests.description: If the diff touches tests, the review must do more than acknowledge their existence — it must call out the gap explicitly. Bare 'test' is excluded from the keyword list; the response has to name the kind of coverage missing.
tests.input: Review this PR: it adds a new function plus two unit tests that exercise only the happy path.

tests.description: Reviews that catch only formatting (extra newline, indentation) when the diff has real design content should be flagged as shallow. The not_regex assertion catches the model concluding with approval, but tolerates quoting the input's 'Approve.' token.
tests.input: Review this PR: 'Looks good. Nit: extra blank line at the end of handler.ts. Approve.' The diff itself adds a 200-line authentication module.

tests.description: Praise without a reference to the diff is filler, not a review. The skill must flag this and demand specifics tied to actual frames in the change.
tests.input: Please review this PR review: 'Looks clean, nicely done, ship it!' The diff itself is a 150-line refactor of the payments retry loop.

tests.description: Performance claims without measurement are soft-fail speculation; the skill must demand evidence (benchmark, profile, measurement) before flagging perf concerns on a hot path.
tests.input: Review this PR: it touches a hot loop in the request handler. The reviewer is tempted to write 'this could be slow under load.' Decide what to surface.
